title: Wyoming vs. Delaware vs. New Mexico LLC in 2026: Which State Actually Makes Sense for Non-US Residents?
content:
# Wyoming vs. Delaware vs. New Mexico LLC in 2026: Which State Actually Makes Sense for Non-US Residents?

Choosing the wrong state for your LLC costs you money every year and can create tax headaches you never expected. Here is an honest breakdown of Wyoming, Delaware, and New Mexico for non-US residents in 2026.

---

## The Three Contenders at a Glance

| Feature | Wyoming | Delaware | New Mexico |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annual Fee | $60 (min.) | $175+ franchise tax (corps); $300 (LLCs) | $0 |
| Formation Fee | ~$100 | ~$90 | ~$50 |
| Owner Privacy | Very High | Moderate | Very High |
| Court System | Standard | Specialized (Chancery) | Standard |
| Registered Agent Required | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Best For | Privacy + low cost | VC-backed or institutional | Ultra-lean, zero maintenance |

> **Note:** Annual fees listed are base figures for 2026. Delaware's franchise tax structure varies by entity type and calculation method. For LLCs and partnerships, the minimum is $300. For corporations, the minimum is $175 under the Authorized Shares Method or $400 under the Assumed Par Value Capital Method. It can spike sharply depending on your structure, so budget carefully.

---

## Wyoming LLC: The Workhorse for Non-Residents

Wyoming became the gold standard for non-US residents years ago and it still holds up in 2026.

**What makes it attractive:**

- No state income tax
- No state corporate tax
- Member names are not required on public filings
- Charging order protection is among the strongest in the US
- Annual fee starts at $60, calculated on assets in Wyoming (typically just $60 for most small LLCs)

**The reality on privacy:** Wyoming does not publicly list member or manager names in its standard database. You file an annual report with a registered agent address. That matters if you are operating in industries or regions where ownership visibility creates personal or business risk.

**One honest limitation:** Wyoming does require a registered agent with a physical Wyoming address. Budget $50 to $150 per year for a quality registered agent service.

**Who should choose Wyoming:** Non-US residents running service businesses, e-commerce, consulting, or SaaS with no plans to raise institutional capital. It is the most balanced option across cost, privacy, and compliance simplicity.

---

## Delaware LLC: When the Reputation Costs More Than It Delivers

Delaware is the default recommendation from US lawyers and startup advisors. For most non-residents building online businesses, that reputation does not translate into real value.

**What Delaware actually offers:**

- The Court of Chancery: a specialized business court with predictable, sophisticated rulings
- High institutional familiarity (investors and VCs expect it)
- Flexible LLC operating agreement language
- A large body of established case law

**Where it falls short for non-residents:**

- Delaware LLCs pay a minimum $300 annual tax. Corporations face a minimum of $175 (Authorized Shares Method) or $400 (Assumed Par Value Capital Method), and those figures can climb steeply based on share structure or capitalization.
- If you are not raising venture capital or dealing with US institutional investors, the Court of Chancery is irrelevant to your operations
- You still need a registered agent in Delaware ($50 to $200 per year)
- No meaningful privacy advantage over Wyoming

> **Note:** Delaware makes perfect sense if you plan to convert to a C-Corp for fundraising later, or if a US investor or accelerator specifically requires it. Otherwise, the annual cost premium is not justified.

**Who should choose Delaware:** Non-residents who are building a startup intending to raise US venture capital, take on institutional partners, or issue equity to employees via a structure that may later need to convert to a C-Corp.

---

## New Mexico LLC: The Underrated Zero-Cost Option

New Mexico does not get enough attention. It is quietly one of the most practical states for lean, low-overhead foreign-owned LLCs.

**Key advantages:**

- No annual report required
- No annual fee
- Formation cost is roughly $50 and you are done
- Members and managers are not required to appear in public records
- Perpetual existence without yearly filings

**What this means practically:** Once you form a New Mexico LLC, your ongoing compliance costs are limited to your registered agent fee and federal tax filing. There is no state-level renewal bureaucracy eating into your margins each year.

**On registered agent costs:** Commercial registered agent services in New Mexico typically run $99 to $300 per year. Some providers advertise lower introductory rates, but standalone annual renewal fees generally start around $99. Factor that into your budget from day one.

**Limitations to know:**

- Less name recognition with banks and payment processors, though this is rarely a dealbreaker
- Thinner body of case law compared to Delaware
- No specialized business court

> **Note:** New Mexico LLCs are legitimate and fully functional. The obscurity is a feature for privacy, not a sign of weakness. Banks like Mercury, Relay, and Wise Business accept New Mexico LLCs without issue in 2026.

**Who should choose New Mexico:** Non-residents launching their first US LLC on a tight budget, solo operators wanting maximum privacy and minimum ongoing cost, or anyone testing a business model before committing to higher-fee states.

---

## The Decision Framework

Ask yourself three questions:

1. **Am I raising US venture capital or taking institutional investment?** Yes: Delaware. No: continue.
2. **Do I want minimal ongoing costs and zero annual reports?** Yes: New Mexico.
3. **Do I want strong legal protections, moderate costs, and broad bank acceptance?** Yes: Wyoming.

Most non-US residents reading this will land on Wyoming or New Mexico. Both are solid. The difference is roughly $60 per year and a slight edge in legal infrastructure that rarely matters for online businesses under $1 million in revenue.
